paragraphs.text: The Hobbit (stylized as Magic: The Gathering® | The Hobbit™ ) is a Magic: The Gathering expansion in the Universes Beyond series, based on the novel of the same name by J.R.R. Tolkien. It was released on August 14, 2026. The set was designed with Pick-Two Draft (4-player draft) in mind.

The Hobbit is the second Magic set based on Tolkien's Middle-earth , after The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth , and the 113th expansion overall. Wizards of the Coast first teased the set with a short animated video wishing happy birthday to Bilbo Baggins , which led to speculation of a new Middle-earth crossover product. The set was officially announced four days later at MagicCon Atlanta 2025. It was created in close cooperation with Middle-earth Enterprises , the firm which owns the rights.
The main Standard -legal set uses the code HOB. Alternate card frames have a different card number than the original version.

The related non-Standard code is HOC ( The Hobbit Commander , or rather The Hobbit Eternal ); these cards are legal in Commander , Legacy , and Vintage , and reprints remain legal where already legal.

The Hobbit is a smaller set like Marvel's Spider-Man and TMNT . It features 198 regular cards (65 commons, 55 uncommons, 53 rares, 15 mythic rares, 10 basic lands) . It becomes available in Play Boosters , Collector Boosters , the The Hobbit Bundle , a Gift Bundle (released on September 4, 2026), a Draft Night Box, and two Scene Boxes . There are no Commander decks attached to this product.
Dwarven language cards appear only in Collector Boosters in non-foil and traditional foil and always in Dwarvish.

The Hobbit sees the return of various mechanics from its predecessor in the IP, The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth , including Sagas and Amass , although in this set, cards amass Goblins rather than Orcs .

A new spin is put on The Lord of the Rings ' historic mechanic with Storied , which is a mix of historic and ascend . Cards with storied count the number of artifacts, legendary permanents, and Sagas you control, and permanently grant you an enduring story when you control three or more. These cards also have additional effects when you have an enduring story.

Another new mechanic is the keyword action Recruit . When you recruit, you draw a card, discard a card, then create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token if you discarded a nonland card. Similarly to connive , it acts as a smoothing mechanic that also grants its controller some advantage on the board.

Other returning mechanics include Adventure , Ferocious and Landfall . Notably, this is the first set in which Ferocious returns keyworded, although it has been used without the keyword in various other sets. Gift appears as a cameo .
Human , Dwarf , Goblin , Wolf , and Elf typal are all significant themes in the set. There is a minor Bear theme. Hobbit Hole introduces halflingcycling .

The Hobbit is the first premier set since Planar Chaos that does not contain any artifact creature cards. To account for the needs of the set's Limited gameplay that these would usually fill, The Hobbit features three colorless nonartifact creature cards: Long-Bodied Grey Dog , Old Thrush , and Troop of Ponies , all of which fix mana in some way. Not counting Eldrazi or Archaics , this hasn't been done since Ikoria: Lair of Behemoths .
The Hobbit introduces a new kind of deciduous counter, the hone counter . Hone counters are placed on Equipment cards. For each hone counter on an Equipment, its equipped creature gets +1/+0.

As a small set, only five archetypes could be supported. Incidentally, a major event was the Battle of the Five Armies, giving each of them a species to focus on. That led to a mix of enemy and allied colors, as some of the armies had prescribed color pairs.
The Hobbit features the following limited archetypes :
: Humans with recruit
: Wolves with ferocious
: Dwarves with storied
: Elves with landfall

The Hobbit is set in Middle-earth and follows home-loving Bilbo Baggins , the titular hobbit who joins the wizard Gandalf and the thirteen dwarves of Thorin's Company on a quest to reclaim the dwarves' home and treasure from the dragon Smaug . Bilbo's journey takes him from his peaceful rural surroundings into more sinister territory.
For The Hobbit , the battle rules were updated with a new rule (310.8), explaining the state-based action that puts a non-Siege battle into its owner's graveyard when its defense is 0.

This update also added a criterion for mana abilities , stipulating that activated abilities that move cards to or from a library as part of their cost or effect are not mana abilities, even if they make mana.

The set features 40 borderless "Middle-earth classic artist" cards. Each of these cards was originally part of The Lord of the Rings: Tales of Middle-earth and features new borderless artwork by a beloved fantasy artist. Each Play Booster box and Collector Booster box includes a Box Topper that contains 1 traditional foil Middle-earth classic artist card. Non-foil and surge foil Middle-earth classic artist cards appear in Collector Boosters.

The Headliner for this set is Smaug, the Magnificent , which features a gleaming gold foil version, a dragon hoard showcase , a borderless version, and a default version. There will be approximately 500 gleaming gold Smaug, the Magnificent headliner cards printed. This version of Smaug, the Magnificent, appears only in Collector Boosters. Gleaming gold versions of Smaug, the Magnificent can appear in Collector Boosters of any language, but the card will always be in English.

The set features two sets of scene cards with the HOB expansion code, which are available as part of the set's Booster Fun . Two separately sold Scene Boxes each include six borderless foil scene cards with the HOC code. When brought together, the cards form recognizable scenes from the book.
The Hobbit features five Welcome Decks .
The Hobbit was accompanied by the release of a Hobbit themed Secret Lair .

The Battle of the Five Armies Co-op Kit is a supplemental box set designed for co-op play . Thematically and from a marketing perspective it is related to The Hobbit , though it will be released in 2027.

Ordinary Bear is the only vanilla creature in the set. As a sign of the times, being vanilla makes it strictly better than the famous Erhnam Djinn of the Standard Erhnamgeddon deck 24 years ago.
Elvenking's Harper is blue 's first archetypal bear available at common rarity with no downside. At this point, blue remains the only color without a vanilla bear.
Smaug the Magnificent was the most played Hobbit card in Standard immediately following the set's release, appearing in mono-red aggro and Boros Dragons decks.

On May 2, 2026, Donato Giancola pointed out that the recently showcased The One Ring ( The Hobbit Eternal ) appeared to include a flipped cutout of the Ring from a previous borderless version by Marta Nael . The new card merely had the runes removed and was superposed onto a Dan Frazier background. A day later, Dan Frazier admitted using Marta Nael's work as a starting point for the new piece, stating that he had made a mistake in doing so. He and Wizards of the Coast issued a public apology, with Marta being given undisclosed compensation and an artist credit on digital versions of the card.
